A legtöbb vita abból lesz, hogy az ügynö: Most disputes come from the agency and the client meaning different things by “lead”. What doesn't count: a wrong number, the same person twice, competitors, job seekers, anyone outside your catchment area, and enquiries with no specific need. The full definition is here.
Az utolsó feltétel a leggyakrabban kihag: The last condition is the one most often skipped. If the ad and the landing page show the starting price, the price isn't a surprise on the phone — and you don't spend twenty conversations with people it was never going to suit.

Miért nincs fix ár?: Why isn't there a fixed price?
A Google Ads aukciós rendszer. Nem egy f: Google Ads is an auction. You don't pay a fixed “list price”; you compete with other advertisers for every single click. The price of a click depends on three main things:
<strong>Verseny:</strong> minél többen l: Competition: the more advertisers bidding on the same keyword, the more expensive it gets. A legal or insurance keyword can be many times the price of a niche product's.
<strong>Minőségi mutató (Quality Score):: Quality Score: Google rewards a relevant ad and a good landing page — you get a better position for less. A low-quality advertiser pays a premium.
<strong>Célzás:</strong> hol, mikor, mil: Targeting: where, when, on what device and to whom you appear. The same keyword costs differently in a capital city at peak time than in a rural area at dawn.
A Google-ben napi büdzsét állítasz be ka: In Google you set a daily budget per campaign. The system tries to hold to it day by day (it can go over in the short term, but evens out by the end of the month). The practical formula is simple: daily budget × 30.4 ≈ monthly spend. If your monthly budget is 150 000 HUF, that's about 5 000 HUF a day.
Hol csorog el a pénz feleslegesen?: Where does the money leak away?
A legtöbb fiókban nem a büdzsé kevés — h: In most accounts the budget isn't too small — it drains in the wrong places. The most common money pits:
<strong>Nincs konverziómérés.</strong> H: No conversion tracking. If you don't measure what produces a purchase or an enquiry, you're bidding blind. This is the most expensive mistake.
<strong>Nincsenek kizáró kulcsszavak.</s: No negative keywords. You're paying for searches that never buy (“free”, “jobs”, “DIY”, and so on).
<strong>Túl tág egyezés.</strong> A szél: Match types too broad. A broad-match keyword shows against a huge number of irrelevant searches if there's no tracking and no exclusions alongside it.
<strong>Gyenge céloldal.</strong> Hiába: A weak landing page. A good ad counts for nothing if the landing page is slow or unclear — the click costs money but produces no client.
<strong>„Beállít és elfelejt\".</strong>: “Set it and forget it”. The auction and the competition change; without optimisation a campaign slowly decays.
